Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Role Overview:

We’re looking for a senior engineer to help build, maintain and evolve the training framework that powers our frontier-scale language models. This role sits at the intersection of large-scale training, distributed systems, and HPC infrastructure. You will design and maintain the core components that enable fast, reliable, and scalable model training — and build the tooling that connects research ideas to thousands of GPUs.

If you enjoy working across the full stack of ML systems, this role gives you the opportunity and autonomy to have massive impact by working on projects such as:

- Building a high-performance data loading and caching pipeline.

- Implementing performance profiling across the ML systems stack

- Developing internal metrics and monitoring for training runs.

- Building reproducibility and regression testing infrastructure.

- Developing a performant fault-tolerant distributed checkpointing system.

Key Responsibilities:

- Build and own the training framework responsible for large-scale LLM training.

- Design distributed training abstractions (data/tensor/pipeline parallelism, FSDP/ZeRO strategies, memory management, checkpointing).

- Improve training throughput and stability on multi-node clusters (e.g., GB200/300, AMD, H200/100).

- Develop and maintain tooling for monitoring, logging, debugging, and developer ergonomics.

- Collaborate closely with infra teams to ensure our cluster, container environments, and hardware configurations support high-performance training.

- Investigate and resolve performance bottlenecks across the ML systems stack.

- Build robust systems that ensure reproducible, debuggable, large-scale runs.

Qualifications:

- Strong engineering experience in large-scale distributed training or HPC systems.
Deep familiarity with JAX internals, distributed training libraries, or custom kernels/fused ops.

- Experience with multi-node cluster orchestration (Slurm, Ray, Kubernetes, or similar).

- Comfort debugging performance issues across CUDA/NCCL, networking, IO, and data pipelines.

- Experience working with containerized environments (Docker, Singularity/Apptainer).

- A track record of building tools that increase developer velocity for ML teams.

- Excellent judgment around trade-offs: performance vs complexity, research velocity vs maintainability.

- Strong collaboration skills — you’ll work closely with infra, research, and deployment teams.

Any of the following would also be good to have for this role:

- Experience with training LLMs or other large transformer architectures.

- Contributions to ML frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, DeepSpeed, Megatron, xFormers, etc.).

- Familiarity with evaluation and serving frameworks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, custom KV caches).

- Experience with data pipeline optimization, sharded datasets, or caching strategies.

- Background in performance engineering, profiling, or low-level systems.

Bonus: paper at top-tier venues (such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AIStats, MLSys, JMLR, AAAI, Nature, COLING, ACL, EMNLP).

Working Location:
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

- A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

- Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

- RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

- 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

- Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

- 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

- Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

- Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

- For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

- For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

- Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. jobs.description:
Generative AI is transforming how people work, but here's the unsolved problem: how do you give an AI assistant to 100,000 employees while keeping the right guardrails in place? And what if an administrator could just tell the system what they want in plain language, instead of navigating a maze of settings?

THE ROLE

We are looking for a Front-End Engineer II who wants to work at the intersection of AI interaction design and enterprise-scale software. You will own the design and delivery of interfaces ranging from conversational AI configuration flows to data-rich dashboards and policy management UIs.

Challenges you'll tackle:

- Agentic and conversational UX: chat-based interfaces where administrators express intent in natural language and the system translates it into precise configurations

- Hybrid interaction models: seamlessly blending conversational AI with structured UI controls, knowing when chat is the right modality vs. a visual editor

- Complex interactive systems: policy builders with hierarchical inheritance, permission matrices, and conditional logic that must remain intuitive at scale

- Data-dense visualization: usage dashboards, audit views, and analytics surfacing actionable insights from millions of events

ABOUT AMAZON QUICK

Amazon Quick is a generative AI-powered assistant that empowers employees to be more productive by answering questions, generating content, providing summaries, and completing tasks, all securely grounded in enterprise data. Quick serves some of the world's largest enterprises, with deployments spanning hundreds of thousands of users.

Key job responsibilities
1. Own end-to-end feature delivery from technical design through implementation, testing, and production release.

2. Build innovative interaction patterns: natural language configuration interfaces, agentic chat UX, policy editors, and observability dashboards using React, TypeScript, and AWS Cloudscape Design System.

3. Define UX for a new problem space. Work with talented UX designers and product managers to invent interaction patterns that don't yet exist in the industry. You won't just implement specs; you'll shape what the product should be.

4. Drive front-end quality with clean, well-tested code, comprehensive tests, and operational ownership of your features in production.

5. Contribute to front-end architecture: component design, state management patterns, performance optimization, and reusable abstractions.

6. Collaborate cross-functionally with backend engineers, applied scientists, and security teams to bring complex capabilities to life through intuitive interfaces.

About the team
The Governance Platform is the control layer for Amazon Quick. We build the interfaces that customers use to manage policies, configure access, and monitor AI usage across their organization. We're pioneering a new approach: natural language and agentic chat interfaces that let administrators configure complex systems conversationally, alongside rich visual UIs for when precision and overview are needed. This space is nascent. There is no established playbook for how AI governance UX should work. The patterns you build here will help define how the entire industry thinks about administering AI systems at scale.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to own engineering excellence across the North American Stores (NAS) organization, the teams behind Amazon's shopping and returns experience. NAS is accountable for a widening set of cross-cutting mandates that central teams set, spanning infrastructure cost, operational resilience, security remediation, how fast and safely we ship, and how we protect customer data. These arrive in-year, on the same teams and the same capacity, and this role is how NAS stays ahead of all of them at once. You will stand up and run a new program that holds the organization to a single high bar across five domains and gives leadership one honest read on the whole surface.

You will operate in an ambiguous, high-visibility space that demands deep technical judgment and the ability to build consensus without direct authority. Working with our most senior engineers, you will set the bar for each domain, decompose a sprawling excellence surface into a small set of measurable goals, and drive teams across every organization in NAS to meet them. You will be NAS's single point of contact to the central organizations that set the work, carrying our position and tradeoffs back to them so we shape the mandates rather than only absorb them, and negotiating scope and timelines when a new goal lands mid-cycle.

This role changes how NAS operates, from reacting to each new mandate cold to running from a standing state of readiness, through a model where every organization has one point of contact, each domain has a technical owner, and an automated scorecard surfaces risk before it becomes a miss. You will invent the mechanisms that make excellence a leadership expectation rather than a reporting tax, and you will own the monthly review where the leaders who run the teams engage directly on tradeoffs and path to green.

Key job responsibilities
Program Strategy and Scorecard Ownership - Define and run the end-to-end engineering excellence program across five domains: infrastructure efficiency, operational excellence, cross-cutting mandates, builder enablement, and privacy. Own a single flagship goal per domain and the one scorecard that reports all five to NAS leadership, so the organization has one honest read on the whole surface rather than five disconnected ones.

Central-Team Liaison and Mandate Negotiation - Be NAS's single point of contact to the central organizations that set the work, including SDO, the S-Team, Infosec, and Amazon Privacy Services. Carry NAS's position and tradeoffs back to them, negotiate scope and timelines when a mandate arrives in-year, and represent NAS in central roadmaps so the organization shapes the requirements rather than only receiving them.

Cross-Organizational Leadership and Influence - Drive the domain goals to closure across every organization in NAS, in teams you do not own and without direct authority. Responsible for leading a team of domain owners who are themselves senior technical program managers and engineers, and hold senior managers and their teams to the bar, running an operating model where each domain has a technical owner and each organization supplies a point of contact so one program covers the full surface.

Mechanism Invention and Simplification - Decompose an ambiguous, sprawling excellence surface into a small set of measurable bars, and invent the mechanisms that move them. Partner with Principal and Senior Principal Engineers to set each bar at the right altitude, and retire the mechanisms that add process without moving the outcome.

Review Cadence and Executive Communication - Own the in-person monthly review that NAS technical leaders are required to attend, where leaders engage directly on at-risk organizations and path to green. Produce the monthly flash to leadership covering status, risks, and decisions across all five domains, translating a wide surface into the few things leaders need to act on.

A day in the life
Your day spans the five domains NAS is measured on and the leaders who own them. You start with the program scorecard, looking for the organizations trending off their bar, then pull the domain owners and each org's point of contact together to work root cause and path to green. You meet with a central program team to negotiate the scope or timeline of a mandate that landed mid-cycle, and you carry that back to NAS leaders so no team absorbs it cold. You partner with Principal and Senior Principal Engineers to set or sharpen a domain bar, and with technical leaders across the organization to sequence the work against their capacity. You close by preparing the monthly flash that gives leadership one honest read across all five domains, and by running the in-person review where the leaders who own the teams engage directly on the tradeoffs and decisions in front of them.

About the team
The Fashion & Fitness Tech organization is on a mission to make Amazon the most-loved fashion destination globally through technology. Our team enhances customer satisfaction and operational excellence across the e-commerce platform. We analyze the shopping experience to help customers find the right products and make confident purchasing decisions. Through data-driven insights and cross-functional collaboration with product, operations, merchandising, and technology teams, we identify and implement improvements that reduce friction and increase post-purchase satisfaction. Our work impacts millions of customers while contributing to business profitability and sustainable growth.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Strategic Finance Lead to help lead the economics of our AI products. In this role, you will be a key partner to our product, inference, and data teams, providing financial expertise to optimize model spend and drive pricing and margin decisions.

In this role, you'll develop deep expertise in the unit economics of AI products, from per-request serving cost to consolidated product-level margin across our portfolio. You'll build the models that inform Perplexity's pricing, packaging, and model-deployment decisions, own the product-margin methodology that reconciles revenue and inference cost from production data, and translate complex model economics into clear financial narratives for leadership.

This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance and AI product strategy, and who is energized by building frameworks from scratch in a fast-moving environment.

This position is based in San Francisco and requires in-person attendance 2-3 days per week.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Finance lead for inference and model spend, including budgeting, monthly forecasting, variance analysis, and financial plan maintenance

- Build and maintain product-margin models across the product portfolio, reconciling revenue, serving cost, and gross margin from production usage data

- Develop deep expertise in model provider contracts, pricing structures, and cost drivers, and surface optimization opportunities across the model portfolio and routing mix

- Serve as subject matter expert for product unit economics, owning source of truth on cost per request, margin by product and tier, and customer-segment and feature-level economics

- Own the consolidated model-cost forecast, translating product roadmaps and model transitions into forward-looking spend and margin trajectories

- Analyze the margin impact of pricing, packaging, and model-deployment decisions, distilled into a framework for product and pricing strategy

- Partner closely with product, inference, and data engineering to understand how usage and serving cost scale, and translate those technical dynamics into financial frameworks

YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

- Exceptional analytical skills with an ability to synthesize data into compelling insights and develop complex financial operating models

- Extraordinary problem-solving and critical thinking abilities to develop new frameworks for assessing product margin and unit economics in a rapidly evolving industry

- Attention to detail and patience for getting to the source of truth on complex and interconnected usage, revenue, and cost data

- Comfort working cross-functionally and are adept at communicating complex financial information to non-finance audiences

- Sound commercial judgment across pricing, packaging, discounting, and the tradeoffs between growth and margin

- A proven track record of partnering with technical and product teams to drive financial optimization initiatives

- A bias toward action, strong work ethic, and experience driving operational outcomes under tight timelines

- Background in AI, ML, or consumption-based business models with complex cost structures

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 4+ years of experience in strategic finance, private equity, growth equity, consulting, or investment banking, preferably with software or AI product experience

- Experience in AI or LLM product financial management, including direct work with model providers or inference platforms

- Deep expertise in usage-based pricing, subscription economics, and gross-margin and COGS attribution by customer and model family

- Experience with model serving economics, including how latency, throughput, and token usage flow through to margin performance

- Proficiency with financial modeling tools
